record.original_question: Can the Newton-identity method described in the chapter be generalized so as to recover the minimum-weight codewords of generalized Reed–Muller codes of arbitrary order, or at least yield a shorter proof than the classical arguments?

evidence.quote: We cannot say, at present, if our method which leads to the description of the set of minimum weight codewords of GRM codes of some orders (Theorem 3.18) can be generalized to GRM codes of any order.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a prime power and $m\ge 1$ an integer. For an integer $r$ with $0\le r\le m(q-1)$, the generalized Reed–Muller code $\mathrm{GRM}_q(r,m)$ of order $r$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear code consisting of the evaluation vectors $(f(x))_{x\in\mathbb{F}_q^m}$ of all polynomials $f\in\mathbb{F}_q[X_1,\dots,X_m]$ of total degree at most $r$ in which each variable appears with degree at most $q-1$. The minimum distance of $\mathrm{GRM}_q(r,m)$ is known, and the set of minimum-weight codewords has been characterized by classical arguments (Delsarte–Goethals–MacWilliams and subsequent work).

A "Newton-identity method" approach proceeds as follows. Identify a codeword $c\in\mathrm{GRM}_q(r,m)$ with its associated polynomial $f$, and let $Z(f)\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^m$ be the zero set of $f$. Using Newton's identities relating the power sums $p_k=\sum_{x\in Z(f)} x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_m^{a_m}$ (over appropriate monomials) to the elementary symmetric functions of the coordinates of points in $Z(f)$, together with the constraints imposed on these power sums by the degree restriction on $f$, one derives algebraic identities forcing the structure of $Z(f)$ when $|Z(f)|$ is maximal (equivalently, when $\mathrm{wt}(c)$ equals the minimum distance). This method has been shown to recover the description of the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathrm{GRM}_q(r,m)$ for certain orders $r$.

Question: Can the Newton-identity method be extended to recover the complete description of the set of minimum-weight codewords of $\mathrm{GRM}_q(r,m)$ for every order $r$ with $1\le r\le m(q-1)-1$? More modestly, does there exist such an extension yielding a proof of the classification of minimum-weight codewords of $\mathrm{GRM}_q(r,m)$ strictly shorter than the classical proofs?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search reveals continued activity on minimum-weight and higher-weight codewords of generalized Reed–Muller codes (e.g., work on second/third/fourth weights and algorithmic approaches using Newton's identities and Gröbner bases), but no source clearly states that the Newton-identity method has been generalized to recover minimum-weight codewords of GRM codes of arbitrary order, nor that this has been ruled out. Status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the codewords of generalized Reed-Muller codes reaching the fourth weight
status_evidence.snippet: Studies higher-weight codewords of GRM codes, indicating ongoing partial progress beyond minimum weight.
status_evidence.claim: Research on classifying low-weight codewords of GRM codes is ongoing for specific orders/weights.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Algorithms for Constructing Minimum-Weight Codewords
status_evidence.snippet: Uses Newton's identities and elimination theory for minimum distance and minimum-weight codeword problems in BCH codes.
status_evidence.claim: Newton-identity techniques continue to be developed, but applied to BCH codes rather than a complete generalization to all-order GRM codes.

status_evidence.title: Identifying codewords in general Reed-Muller codes and determining their weights
status_evidence.snippet: Methods to determine weights of codewords in Reed-Muller codes of arbitrary lengths and orders.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses weights in Reed-Muller codes of arbitrary order, but does not explicitly resolve the Newton-identity generalization question.
